info.name: Beat-x API
info.description:
# BeatX Backend API

## Authentication
All protected routes use a **Bearer token** (`{{accessToken}}`). Run **Auth → Login** first — the test script auto-saves both tokens to your environment.

## Environment Variables
| Variable | Set by | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `baseUrl` | Manual | e.g. `http://localhost:3000` |
| `accessToken` | Login script | JWT access token (short-lived) |
| `refreshToken` | Login script | JWT refresh token (long-lived) |
| `podcasterId` | Manual | ObjectId of a Podcaster document |
| `showId` | Manual | ObjectId of a PodcastShow document |
| `episodeId` | Manual | ObjectId of a PodcastEpisode document |
| `uploadId` | Manual | UUID returned by POST /files/upload (for SSE progress) |

## Response Envelope
Every response is wrapped:
```json
{
  "status": true,
  "message": "...",
  "data": { ... },
  "timestamp": "ISO-8601",
  "path": "/route",
  "metadata": { "duration": "4ms" }
}
```

## Roles
`user` (default) · `moderator` · `admin` — role is encoded in the JWT and checked server-side.

## File Uploads
All file uploads go through `POST /files/upload` or `POST /files/upload/batch`. The `purpose` field determines allowed MIME types, max file size, and whether admin role is required.

request.description:
Authenticates with email + password. The test script automatically saves `accessToken` and `refreshToken` to your Postman environment.

> Email must be verified before login is allowed.
Issues a fresh `accessToken` + `refreshToken` pair using a valid refresh token. The test script auto-updates both environment variables.

Sets a new password using the email + OTP obtained from the forgot-password flow. The OTP is re-verified server-side before the change is applied. All active sessions are invalidated after a successful reset.

request.description: Returns the full profile of the currently authenticated user.
Returns the full profile of the currently authenticated user.

`artistIds`: array of User ObjectIds — unique, valid Mongo IDs (`ArrayUnique`, `IsMongoId({ each: true })`). Unlike Favorite Genres there is **no minimum size** — an empty array is allowed and clears the list. Every id must belong to a User with an `ArtistVerification.status === 'approved'`, checked via a `countDocuments` match against the submitted count; otherwise `400 Bad Request` ("One or more selected artists are not approved"). Replaces `favoriteArtists` entirely (not a merge).

Updates the user's name, phone, and/or avatar. All fields are optional.

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | max 100 characters |
| `phone` | string | international format, e.g. `+8801800000000` |
| `avatarKey` | string | S3 object key from `POST /files/upload` with `purpose: user_avatar` |

**Avatar upload workflow:**
1. `POST /files/upload` with `purpose: user_avatar` → get `key`
2. `PATCH /users/profile` with `{ avatarKey: key }`

Changes password for local-auth accounts. Social login accounts (Google, Facebook) cannot use this endpoint.

**`newPassword` rules:** min 8 chars · at least one uppercase · at least one number · must differ from current password · `confirmPassword` must match.
Returns the user's app settings object.

Permanently deletes the account. Password confirmation is required. Social-login accounts cannot use this endpoint.

No `@Roles` restriction and no explicit `@UseGuards` — only the global `JwtAuthGuard` applies, so (per the collection-level auth-model note) any authenticated user can call this, but it still requires a Bearer token today.

Returns every `User` whose linked `ArtistVerification.status` is `approved`, each shaped as:
```json
{ "_id": "...", "name": "...", "avatar": "...", "stageName": "...|null", "artistAvatar": "...|null" }
```
`stageName` / `artistAvatar` are pulled from that artist's verification `personalInfo.stageName` / `mediaAssets.profilePictureUrl`. Copy an `_id` into `artistId` to use with *Update Favorite Artists*.

Explicit `@UseGuards(JwtAuthGuard)` (redundant with the global guard). Returns the caller's favorites in one call:
```json
{ "favoriteGenres": [ { "_id": "...", "name": "..." } ], "favoriteArtists": [ { "_id": "...", "name": "...", "avatar": "..." } ] }
```
`favoriteGenres` is fully populated; `favoriteArtists` is populated with only `name` and `avatar` projected.

request.description:
Server-Sent Events stream — open before or during chunk uploads.
No Authorization header required (uploadId acts as the bearer).

Event shape:
  { uploadId, uploadedChunks, totalChunks, percent, status }
  status: 'uploading' → percent increases each chunk
  status: 'done'      → percent: 100, result: <created resource>
  status: 'failed'    → upload failed, retry or abort
  status: 'aborted'   → upload was cancelled

Connection closes automatically when status is done/failed/aborted.

NOTE: Postman does not natively render SSE streams.
Use a browser EventSource or curl:
  curl -N {{baseUrl}}/uploads/{{uploadId}}/progress

formdata.description: draft | scheduled | active | archived — defaults to active (goes live immediately). Ignored if scheduledAt is set (forced to 'scheduled').

Optional — ISO date-time in the future, e.g. 2026-08-01T09:00:00.000Z. When set, the podcast is created hidden (status auto-forced to 'scheduled') and a cron job flips it to 'active' at that moment — no manual publish step needed.

request.description:
Callable by an admin, or by an artist whose ArtistVerification.status is 'approved' — otherwise 403. The podcast's ownerId is set to the caller automatically.

Scheduling: enable the 'scheduledAt' field with a future ISO date-time to publish later instead of immediately. The backend rejects a past/invalid date, and rejects status=scheduled sent without scheduledAt (400 in both cases).
403 if the podcast is owned by someone else (admin can view any).

Editorial fields (isFeatured, isTrending, trendDirection, ownerId) are NOT accepted here — use Admin — Update Podcast for those.

Scheduling: send { "scheduledAt": "2026-08-01T09:00:00.000Z" } to (re)schedule — status is auto-forced to 'scheduled'. Send { "status": "active" } (without scheduledAt) to cancel an existing schedule and publish immediately, or { "status": "draft" } to unpublish/unschedule.

Example: schedule an existing podcast to go live at a future date/time. status is auto-set to 'scheduled' (hidden from all public endpoints) until the PODCAST_SCHEDULED_PUBLISH cron job (runs every minute) flips it to 'active' once scheduledAt has passed.

400 if scheduledAt is not a valid future date.

episodeNumber is auto-assigned (last episode + 1) — not sent by the client.

The file is buffered and uploaded to R2 in the background — returns { trackingId } immediately.

Track real-time progress via SSE:
  GET /uploads/{{trackingId}}/progress

SSE event shape:
  { status: 'uploading', percent: 0–95 }
  { status: 'done', percent: 100, result: episode }
  { status: 'failed' }

The test script auto-saves trackingId to the collection variable.

If the server is at the concurrency limit (default 3), returns HTTP 429.

Scheduling: enable 'scheduledAt' with a future ISO date-time to hold the episode back — audio still uploads/transcodes right away, it just won't appear on any user-facing endpoint until publish time.
